annotation.title_clean: 49 U.S. Code § 44810 - Airport safety and airspace hazard mitigation and enforcement
annotation.title_en: 49 U.S. Code § 44810 - Airport safety and airspace hazard mitigation and enforcement
annotation.authors_or_issuer: United States Congress (Cornell Legal Information Institute reproduction)
annotation.venue: Cornell Law School Legal Information Institute (US Code)
annotation.summary_en: US statute (49 U.S.C. § 44810) directing the FAA to plan certification and deployment of counter-drone detection and mitigation systems at airports, test them at selected airports, make them grant-eligible, exempt authorised activities from certain criminal statutes, and brief Congress. The authority sunsets September 30, 2028.
key_provisions_or_claims: FAA Administrator must develop a plan to certify and authorize counter-UAS detection and mitigation systems
Systems tested at five airports, including one in the top 10 by boardings
Airport sponsors may use grants to buy certified detection and mitigation systems
Certain criminal statutes (Wiretap Act, CFAA, Pen/Trap) do not apply to authorised activities
Authority ceases September 30, 2028; FAA must not delegate it
